rich_summary: King Janaka explains that many powerful kings once tried to string the sacred bow preserved by his dynasty, hoping to win Sita’s hand, but none succeeded. Their humiliation even led to a year‑long siege of Mithila before Janaka defeated them. At Vishwamitra’s request, the immense bow—so heavy it must be brought on an eight‑wheeled cart by hundreds of men—is presented to Rama. Calmly examining it, Rama lifts the divine weapon with ease and attempts to string it. In the act, his strength shatters the bow with a thunderous crack that shakes the earth and stuns the assembled crowd. Recognizing the miraculous feat, Janaka joyfully declares that his vow is fulfilled and promises Sita in marriage to Rama, sending messengers to invite King Dasaratha to witness the union.

highlight_spans.why: The opening situates the episode within the Bala Kanda, signaling a pivotal mythic turning point in Rama’s youth.
The dramatic moment when Rama effortlessly lifts and draws the bow, revealing his divine strength.
The bow shatters with a thunderous sound that shakes the earth and knocks the crowd senseless—an awe‑filled revelation of Rama’s power.
Janaka acknowledges the miraculous feat and resolves to give Sita to Rama, fulfilling his sacred vow.

top_scenes.scene_text: Rama calmly lifts the colossal divine bow before a vast crowd while sages and King Janaka watch in stunned anticipation.
The bow snaps in Rama’s hands with a thunderclap, shockwaves rippling across the hall as people collapse in awe while only Rama, Lakshmana, and Vishwamitra remain standing.
Hundreds of strong men haul the sacred bow into the court on an eight‑wheeled cart while garlands and sandalwood adorn the massive weapon.
